newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper futures end up in slow trading.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper futures end up in slow trading.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended up in slow trading on Monday due to higher spot copper prices despite last Friday's losses on the London Metal Exchange, traders said.
The most active April 1997 contract ended at an intra-day high of 20,370 yuan ($2,454) per tonne, up 170 yuan. It opened at 20,090 and hit a low of 20,060.
January rose 120 to 20,200, February 220 to 20,320, March 160 to 20,340, May 180 to 20,380 and June 80 to 20,400.
Combined volume fell sharply to 39,390 tonnes from 97,290.
Copper opened lower but buying at low levels pushed prices steadily up before most contracts closed at or near their intra-day highs.
Traders said many investors were wary about the later market trend but firm spot prices supported futures today, despite last Friday's losses on the LME.
"LME losses, which had been expected, had little impact on Shanghai copper today," one trader said. "Firmer spot copper triggered speculative buying and short-covering," he added.
In Shanghai, the current spot copper price is around 20,200 yuan per tonne.
But traders said sharp rises were unlikely in the next few days due to a lack of further positive market-moving news.
"Thin trading volume today indicated a lack of confidence among long position holders," a second trader said.
Analysts expect copper to move between 20,000 and 20,500 in the next few days.
Aluminium ended little changed. January was unchanged at 13,900 yuan per tonne, February did not trade and March rose 20 to 14,120. Combined volume fell to 140 tonnes from 360.
